Package org.locationtech.geomesa.trino.datastore

Class TrinoDataStore

java.lang.Object
org.geotools.data.store.ContentDataStore
org.locationtech.geomesa.trino.datastore.TrinoDataStore
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.geotools.api.data.DataAccess<org.geotools.api.feature.simple.SimpleFeatureType,org.geotools.api.feature.simple.SimpleFeature>, org.geotools.api.data.DataStore
public class TrinoDataStore extends org.geotools.data.store.ContentDataStore
Read-only GeoTools ContentDataStore backed by a Trino/Iceberg catalog, with Z2/XZ2 partition pruning and row-level visibility. The datastore is the trusted intermediary that forwards each caller's authorizations to Trino per query as an extra credential.

Why ContentDataStore and not JDBCDataStore? As of this version, the Trino store is read-only to function primarily as a query engine and does not expose the write-based operations provided by JDBCDataStore. ContentDataStore is the lighter, correct base for a query-only source, it lets us push filter/projection/sort/count/bounds down as Trino SQL (see TrinoFeatureSource), and offers per-request-authenticated connections per query and visibility/entitlement filtering. Because the forwarded authorizations are fixed on a connection at creation, connections are pooled keyed by the normalized auth set (ConnectionPool): requests with the same effective auths reuse connections (see connect(List)).
